correctness.rationale: The graph is cubic on 18 vertices, giving gamma >= 5. The point/line covering inequalities and parallel-line argument classify the exact 18 five-vertex dominating sets. The loss-of-all-selected-neighbors criterion decides each edge deletion. An independent direct LCF C++17 checker and a three-direction-incidence Python checker both produce zero destructive one- or two-edge deletions and exactly 171 destructive triples (18 vertex stars plus 153 disjoint triple matchings); the graph automorphism enumeration certifies orbit sizes 9,18,36,108. Independent model isomorphism and complete finite ranges were replayed. Every destructive triple raises gamma to exactly six by the single-edge restoration lemma.

value.rationale: This canonical cubic symmetric 18-vertex incidence graph has 171 sharp three-edge domination-failure cuts, 153 of which are pairwise disjoint edges and therefore isolate no vertices; this is a nonobvious global vulnerability mechanism beyond the generic 18 edge stars. The four complete automorphism-orbit sizes and exact bound provide a natural finite resilience benchmark, with explicit proof and reproducible exhaustive certificates. The result goes materially beyond the previously known scalar domination number 5.
